data.title: Rain at the Last Station
data.excerpt: He always got off at the same station, even though the person he was waiting for had stopped coming years ago.
content: The rain started just as the last train disappeared from the station.
Raka stood beneath the platform roof, watching the red lights at the back of the train slowly disappear into the mist. In his hand was a blue umbrella he had never actually used.
He already knew that the last train that night was not the one he had been waiting for.
Three years had passed since someone last stood beside him at that station. Three years since a simple promise had been made: "Wait for me here."
At first, Raka came every Friday night. Then every other week. Eventually, he no longer knew why he kept coming.
Perhaps waiting was easier than admitting that someone was never coming back.
Raka looked at his watch. It was almost midnight.
He nodded, then folded the blue umbrella he had been carrying all evening.
As he walked toward the exit, he stopped for a moment and looked back at the platform.
For the first time in three years, he did not expect to see someone standing there.
Outside, the rain was still falling.
Raka opened his blue umbrella and walked home.
